title: Cusco School of painting
summary: The Cusco School was a colonial painting tradition of the Viceroyalty of Peru centred on the Cusco region. It developed in the 17th and 18th centuries, with its style forming after the 1650 earthquake as artists rebuilding churches combined European influences with local elements. Many works were made collectively in workshops, so authorship is often unknown.

uncertainty.note: Kubiak gives the 17th and 18th centuries; MASP says the tradition developed mainly after the 1650 earthquake. Start is 1650 and the start margin reaches back into the 17th century.

importance.justification: The best-known school of colonial Andean religious painting, produced in Cusco workshops.
